newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Wednesday on uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,040 yuan ($2,778) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,140 and hit a low of 22,940 yuan per tonne.
May rose 40 to 23,200, June 50 to 23,150, July fell 20 to 23,020, September was unchanged at 23,000 and October rose 120 to 23,000.
Combined volume fell to 39,860 tonnes from 56,800 tonnes.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices down for most of the session before speculative buying pushed contracts off their lows late in the session.
Traders said investors were mixed about the short-term direction of the market, which caused sharp price fluctuations on Wednesday.
"Many investors traded for quick profits because they don't believe copper will rise or fall sharply in the short term," one trader said.
Firm spot copper prices continued to support early-maturing contracts, traders said. Physical copper is at around 23,300 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
"The thin volume is a good indication that investors prefer to stay on the sidelines for the time being," a second trader said.
Traders said they expect copper to continue to move around the 23,000 yuan level in the short term.
On the aluminium market, only 250 tonnes of May 1997 contract traded. It ended at 15,450 yuan, losing 150 yuan from Tuesday's close.
